observation_summary: The compiler incorrectly infers types when comparing against 'undefined', leading to bogus type mismatch warnings. Specifically, in a test case, the equality check between two 'undefined' types resulted in 'undefined' instead of 'None' (NO_TYPE).
hypothesis: The method responsible for calculating the resulting type pair after an equality check (testForEquality) was returning an incorrect result (null, null) when the equality was determined to be TRUE, instead of returning the appropriate NO_TYPE pair.
prediction: The fix will involve changing the return value in the 'TRUE' case of the equality test switch statement from (null, null) to a pair of NO_TYPE objects.
experiment_rationale: The provided diff shows exactly this change: replacing 'new TypePair(null, null)' with 'new TypePair(noType, noType)' where 'noType' is 'NO_TYPE'. This confirms the logic for handling the equality result was incorrect.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a failure in the computational logic of the type inference engine. The method 'testForEquality' was returning an incorrect representation of the resulting type pair for a TRUE equality condition. This is a procedural/algorithmic error in how the type system handles equality outcomes, not a missing guard (Checking) or a simple variable initialization error (Assignment/Initialization).

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves assigning a value, the root cause is the logic of the equality inference algorithm, not just an incorrect constant initialization.
The issue is not a missing guard or condition, but an incorrect result returned by the existing logic.
